clue.text: Oppose son entering second exam

indicators.note: the son goes into the exam, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken a second time
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son objects to having to sit an exam again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against it, a plain synonym of opposing it.

clue.text: Disprove match official beginning to unveil note

parts.note: a ref is a referee, the official at a match

indicators.note: the beginning of the word unveil is its first letter

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A referee starts to reveal a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute is to prove a claim false, a synonym of disprove.

clue.text: Good man managed artist with queen in port

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
ran means managed, as in running a business
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A virtuous man ran a painter and the monarch in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranraer is a ferry port in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a Scottish ferry port, so an example of a port.

clue.text: Loose rocks above church? Give a cry

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece over the second

parts.note: scree is the loose stone covering a mountain slope

explanation.surface: Falling stones on a slope above a chapel make someone shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To screech is to give a shrill harsh cry.

clue.text: At AGM, it's sadly evidence of shame

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Something embarrassing happened at the annual general meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ATAGMITS, the letters of 'At AGM, it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks of disgrace, signs that someone bears shame.

clue.text: Snobbish aristo, one Dee's diverted

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class person, an aristocrat

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside, so these letters are redirected into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the name written with its s

explanation.surface: A snooty nobleman has had a river redirected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges ONEDEES into EENOSED. The Dee is a British river, which is why diverting it fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is British slang for snobbish or stuck-up.

clue.text: Giant? Uncivilised figure harbouring upcoming trouble

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a Goth was one of the barbarian peoples who invaded Rome

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A barbarian giant is sheltering trouble that is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' signals a reversal because in a down clue the word reads upwards; 'harbouring' then puts the turned word inside the barbarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant slain by David, so his name is used for any giant.

clue.text: A teacher in an advanced state

parts.note: a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher is well along in some process.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front or further on, in an advanced position or state.

clue.text: Independence gained by number in car, wow!

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
my is an exclamation of surprise, like wow

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates the freedom of having their own car.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomy is self-government, the state of being independent.

clue.text: Craze in front part around old city

indicators.note: the front part is wrapped round the old city, one piece enclosing the other

parts.note: the fore is the front part of something, as of a ship
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A frenzy breaks out in the front section near an ancient settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is a public frenzy or uproar, close to a craze in the sense of a sudden mania.

clue.text: A fellow speaking easily having wealth

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
someone fluent speaks with ease

explanation.surface: A man who talks smoothly and is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, so it fits a description of someone having wealth.

clue.text: State in which criminal teen's seen

indicators.note: criminal implies something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the word written with its s, giving five letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: The place where a young offender was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TEENSSEEN; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA, an example of a state.

clue.text: Group with article escorted, we hear, to explain background

parts.note: a set is a group
the is the definite article

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to see someone home is to escort them, so escorted gives seen

explanation.surface: A party with a chaperone is introduced at the start of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. To see someone off or home is to escort them, so 'escorted' is SEEN, which sounds like SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the scene is to describe the background or context before the main action.

clue.text: A university haunt for poet

parts.note: a den is a favourite haunt or hideaway

explanation.surface: A campus hangout frequented by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Mother in a hat's drunk tonic

indicators.note: drunk suggests reeling and confusion, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the four words written out in full, with the s of the last

explanation.surface: Mum, wearing a hat, has knocked back a gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the thirteen letters of 'Mother in a hat's'; 'tonic' looks like part of the drink but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, a boost or stimulus is called a shot in the arm, just as a tonic is something invigorating.

clue.text: A name around trade union followed by a learner? It's the truth

indicators.note: the name wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: to cite is to name, as when citing a source

indicators.note: the union comes first and the next pieces after it

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A named union official and a trainee claim to be telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' splits the name after its first letter to take in the union, a and learner. 'It's' is a link, and the answer is a French borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Actualité is a borrowing from French meaning factual truth or reality.

clue.text: Neat chaps possibly caught leaving some game

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
leaving means the caught letter departs from the fodder

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Tidy men may be arrested and leave a shooting party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes C from NEATCHAPS and 'possibly' rearranges the remaining NEATHAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasant is a game bird shot for sport, so an example of game.

clue.text: Tree has, say, grey fruit around trunk

indicators.note: the fruit is placed round about the trunk, next to it in the answer

parts.note: a grey is a horse of that colour, so a grey is an example of a horse
the chest is the trunk of the body
a nut is a fruit

explanation.surface: A tree bearing fruit has a grey bark round its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks grey as an example: a grey is a horse. 'around' places the fruit beside the trunk rather than enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a large deciduous tree that bears conkers, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Captivate English conservationists with prince? About right

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation body

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the prince goes round the right

parts.note: Hal is Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: An English heritage group with a royal is told that they are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to hold someone spellbound, to captivate them.

clue.text: Confound leaders of notorious offenders nearby? A positive sign

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their first letters

parts.note: plus is the positive sign in arithmetic

explanation.surface: Notorious criminals close at hand are a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle them, to confound them.

clue.text: Slithery sort outwardly pretty though overblown

indicators.note: outwardly means taking just the outside letters of each word

explanation.surface: Something that looks attractive but is exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of each word give PY, TH and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a large snake, a slithering creature.

clue.text: Watchful prince missing bishop

indicators.note: missing means the bishop is absent, taken out of the name

parts.note: Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, Prince Albert
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A vigilant royal is without a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means watchful and on guard, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Metal worker not initially for senior church figure

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a welder joins pieces of metal

explanation.surface: A metalworker who has lost the first letter becomes a church elder.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay officer in Presbyterian and other churches.

clue.text: Inactive name found in faltering trade? Yes

indicators.note: the name is placed within the scrambled letters
faltering suggests unsteadiness, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stagnant business is a sign of idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faltering' rearranges the letters of trade and Yes, and 'found in' places the name abbreviation among them; the question mark suits the surface's query.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes someone who sits a lot and takes little exercise, so inactive.

clue.text: Early end to ramble around island

indicators.note: to ramble around is to wander aimlessly, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A walk round an island finishes before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramble around' rearranges EARLYEND; 'to' is a link. Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, an example of an island.

clue.text: Reportedly, do away with wintry transport

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to slay is to kill, to do away with someone

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone has abolished a winter vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn over snow, so a form of transport used in winter.

clue.text: Guide on boat restricting hour for exciting film

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the hour is held inside the guide

parts.note: a tiller is the lever used to steer a boat

explanation.surface: A helmsman on a vessel is limited to sixty minutes for a gripping movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a film or novel full of suspense and excitement.

clue.text: Group of Easterners at back of vessel

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A party of people from the East sit at the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for at or towards the stern, the rear of a ship.
